attributes.law_screen: claim.law.offsetof-rename-can-regress-prior-improved-fn: THE governing law for this pass and the reason for its whole shape -- it records that CritterInitGeo specifically regressed (real 63->113 and 63->86) from two independent offsetof conversions on base `c`. Honoured two ways: (a) every hazard function was gated INDIVIDUALLY, never in a TU-wide sweep -- 8 separate gates; (b) the two site groups the law names as having regressed (c+0xF8/0xFC skinMatrix, and the movePathPos/defaultPos/prevMovePathPos block on base `c`) were treated as a HARD VETO and left raw, untouched. The pass instead converted DIFFERENT BASES inside those same functions, which is the finding recorded as the new claim.law.offsetof-hazard-is-per-base-not-per-function. claim.law.offsetof-rename-preserves-protected-web: APPLIED at every one of the 60 sites -- base pointer type and cast type unchanged everywhere, only the displacement constant respelled; zero typed intermediates. claim.law.offsetof-rename-array-member-boundary: SCREENED and then DELIBERATELY TESTED at its boundary -- CritterDoTexmodNode's translation-row triple hangs off `Effects[result].node`, a POINTER field of an ARRAY ELEMENT, which is adjacent to (but not identical to) the array-typed-MEMBER base the law says regresses. A/B'd exactly as the law instructs rather than assumed: GATE OK, so the law's hazard is confirmed to be about array-typed FIELD bases (`obj->arrayfield + N`), not about array indexing in the base expression generally. claim.law.pool-literal-sweep-section-and-lvalue-preconditions: APPLIED as a VETO on the volatile axis -- its precondition (2) records that `*(volatile T*)&lbl_x` is a DELIBERATE existing matching form and an address-taken lvalue that cannot be substituted at all (`&0.0f` is not valid C). claim.law.extern-scalar-read-defeats-fp-literal-hoist explains WHY the form is load-bearing (a mutable extern read is not hoistable across calls, so MWCC reloads it per use, which is the codegen the target wants). Conclusion: those sites are matching machinery, not debt. NOT converted -- see residual. claim.law.embedded-struct-member-whole-tu-cascade: SCREENED, not triggered -- this pass added NO new type declaration to critter.c at all (every record used was already defined in-tree: CritterHitNode, CritterPackedType, and MBObject/Player from headers already included), so there was no new-aggregate gate to take. claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention: SCREENED, not triggered -- no `p += N` load-update web was touched; all conversions were plain single-additive dereferences. claim.law.typed-global-member-vs-view-cast-diverges: SCREENED, respected -- no pre-existing file-local view cast was deleted in favour of a real member type anywhere in this TU. claim.law.local-alias-vs-direct-global-spelling-diverges: SCREENED -- no global's access spelling was unified; every converted site kept its own base expression exactly as written. claim.law.offsetof-rename-isolated-site-outlier: APPLIED as procedure -- defake_gate check --rebuild after every batch, never a spot-check. claim.law.u32-cast-arithmetic-defeats-stmw-fusion: heeded -- no cast TYPE was changed at any site (e.g. hdr+0x124 kept its `*(u8**)` cast even though the field is typed CritterMove*). claim.law.multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing / declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast / write-site-alias-defeats-reload-parity / pointer-walk-array-index-regression / dead-offset-shadow-removal-* / swap-loop-is-record-layout-ground-truth: SCREENED, none of their trigger shapes occurred (no typed alias on a walked base, no pointer-walk-to-array-index rewrite, no shadow accumulator removed, no byte-swap loop touched).

AXES CLOSED WITH CAUSE, do not re-open blindly: (1) THE 19 VOLATILE LABEL SITES ARE NOT DEBT. `*(volatile f32/f64*)&lbl_803464xx` is a deliberate matching idiom (claim.law.pool-literal-sweep-section-and-lvalue-preconditions precondition 2 + claim.law.extern-scalar-read-defeats-fp-literal-hoist): the volatile-qualified read of a mutable pool label is what stops MWCC hoisting the constant out of the loop, which is the target's codegen. It is also un-substitutable in principle since the site takes an ADDRESS. Left untouched by design, not by omission. CritterDropItem's item accesses are already fully converted through the file-local CritterItemView (info/pos/node/minoff). The prior record's 'needs subtype evidence' caveat is correct but moot -- there is nothing here to name.
